newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Extra foreign limit allowed for Shinhan.
newsitem.headline: Extra foreign limit allowed for Shinhan.

text.p: South Korea's Securities Supervisory Board said on Wednesday that 3.13 million, or 2.54 percent, of Shinhan Bank's shares would be newly available for foreign investment from Friday.
The board said in a statement the foreign ownership ceiling for the bank would be 25.54 percent, instead of the 23 percent ceiling in effect for most other companies.
The statement said the extra ceiling had been approved because it was the same stake held by foreign shareholders since the bank's foundation.
The foreign ceiling rose to 23 percent on May 2 from 20 percent on all but two "strategically important" firms, Pohang Iron and Steel and Korea Electric Power.
The ceiling on these two firms was raised to 18 percent at the same time from 15 percent.
